report.source_text: On the 4th day of hospitalization, the patient was discharged and referred for further surgical and oncological treatment. On discharge, the following were recommended: acetylsalicylic acid 75 mg/day, bisoprolol 2.5 mg/day, ramipril 1.25 mg/ day, atorvastatin 20 mg/day, pantoprazole 20 mg/day, supplementation with iron and thyroid hormones, and continuation of the ongoing analgesic chronic therapy. After 4 months, the patient died from cancer.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 62-year-old obese female with history of smoking, hypertension, hypothyroidism, arthritis, and bladder cancer presented with chest pain. On admission, she was hemodynamically stable with BP 110/80 mmHg and no pain. ECG showed normal sinus rhythm and inverted T waves anteriorly and laterally. Cardiac biomarkers revealed markedly elevated troponin I hs at 9552 ng/l. Coronary angiography demonstrated minor atherosclerotic changes without obstructive disease. Left ventriculography showed akinesis of the apex and apical/mid anterior wall with EF 38%. Echocardiography during hospitalization revealed improved LV contractile function with 47% EF and normal valves. The patient was managed conservatively and discharged on standard cardioprotective medications. She was referred for further cancer treatment and died 4 months later from cancer.
